# requireNonEmpty

<link-summary>Returns the value after checking that it is not empty.</link-summary>

<web-summary>requireNonEmpty() — Returns the value after checking that it is not empty. apps-script-utils, English.</web-summary>

<tldr>
<p>Module: <code>lang/base</code> · Since: 1.11.0</p>
</tldr>

```typescript
function requireNonEmpty<T>(
  value: T,
  message: string = "Expected a non-empty value.",
  strict: boolean = false
): T;
```

Emptiness is read per kind: `null` and `undefined`, a string with nothing but whitespace, an array, `Set` or `Map` with no entries, an object with no own keys. `0` and `false` are values, not emptiness.

`isX` and `nonX` answer a question and never interrupt control flow; `requireX` and `requireNonX` hand the value back or throw. The scheme is explained in [](validation-conventions.md).

## Parameters

| Parameter                                                | Type      | Description                                                                                                        |
| :------------------------------------------------------- | :-------- | :----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `value`                                                  | `T`       | The value to validate.                                                                                             |
| `message` _(optional)_ `= "Expected a non-empty value."` | `string`  | The message of the exception. A default is used when omitted.                                                      |
| `strict` _(optional)_ `= false`                          | `boolean` | When `true`, a string counts as empty only if it has no characters at all; by default whitespace is trimmed first. |

## Returns

`T` — the same value, with empty excluded from its type.

## Throws

| Exception                  | Condition           |
| :------------------------- | :------------------ |
| `IllegalArgumentException` | the value is empty. |

## Examples

### What passes and what does not

```javascript
requireNonEmpty(0); // => 0
requireNonEmpty(false); // => false
requireNonEmpty(null); // throws IllegalArgumentException
requireNonEmpty(""); // throws IllegalArgumentException
```
